h: Headlands, lakes and tides at Weston
p: Climbing can make the hands a bit sore, especially for first-timers, so don't be surprised if little ones need a break halfway through. Let them rest, have a drink and then get back on the wall when they're ready. Short nails, comfy clothes and trainers make all the difference, and tying back long hair is a must.

Weston's seafront has more to it than the beach and the pier. Marine Lake, at the northern end of the promenade, is a tidal pool where children can paddle safely even when the sea is far out. Nearby, Knightstone Island has a walkway, cafes and a lovely view across the bay. Weston Museum on Burlington Street tells the story of the town and is a good wet-weather option.

A word of warning: Weston's tide goes out a very long way, and the mud beyond the sand can be dangerous, so stay off it and keep to the beach. For a walk with views, Weston Woods on Worlebury Hill has trails through the trees, and to the south, Uphill village leads on to Brean Down, a National Trust headland with a Victorian fort at the tip and huge views across the Bristol Channel. Sand Point to the north is another lovely spot for a breezy walk. Weston also has a good selection of chippies and cafes along the front for a hearty post-climb refuel, and a stroll along the prom with an ice cream is the classic way to end the day, whatever the season.
